data.split_by: question id, so no question straddles splits
data.leakage_guard: trained on PopQA test-split questions; the dev split used by the Phase 6 ablation is untouched

threshold_protocol.why_not_action_accuracy: val action distribution is 89.3% Correct; maximising action accuracy drifts toward a trivial always-Correct predictor
threshold_protocol.val_finding: NO threshold setting beat the val majority baseline (best 0.8667 vs 0.8933)

prior_placeholder_run_disclosed.note: Scored BETTER on test than the val-selected config. Disclosed, not claimed: selecting it would be tuning on test. The val sweep did not transfer - val is only 75 questions.

crag_comparison.source: Yan et al. 2024, Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation, arXiv:2401.15884v3, Table 4, section 5.5
crag_comparison.crag_setup: T5-large (0.77B) fine-tuned; PopQA; 1399-question test split from Self-RAG; Contriever retrieval, ~10 docs/question
crag_comparison.crag_metric: accuracy of the retrieval ACTION chosen for a retrieved set, not per-chunk grading
crag_comparison.verdict: GATE NOT MET. Our action accuracy (0.8158) is below both CRAG's 0.843 and our own majority-class baseline (0.8750). Because a trivial always-Correct predictor scores 0.875 on this split, beating 0.843 here would not have been a real claim either.

gate.required: beats CRAG-reported grading accuracy; corrective loop fires
